planting.note: Plant divisions or rooted stolons in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this heavily variegated form is less vigorous than plain-leaved selections and benefits from reliable moisture and winter protection.

directions: Plant divisions or rooted stolons in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Its Japanese name, meaning 'kaleidoscopic changes,' describes rounded, scalloped leaves that emerge mostly cream-colored with scattered green splashes, shifting tone through the season in a way more extreme than the widely grown 'Tricolor'. Thin wiry stems carry small white flowers above the foliage in spring, and threadlike red stolons tipped with plantlets spread the clump in the species' characteristic strawberry-like fashion. Because so little chlorophyll is present in the palest leaves, growth is slow and the cultivar is best suited to a sheltered container or shaded rock garden niche rather than open ground.

common_name: Hsitou Silver Strawberry Begonia (Silver-Veined Taiwan Selection)

planting.note: Plant divisions or rooted stolons in spring in moist, rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade; this wild-collected Taiwanese form spreads readily once established.

directions: Plant divisions or rooted stolons in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade. Collected in the Hsitou area of Taiwan, this selection bears rounded, fuzzy, silvery-green leaves with prominent silver-white veins above and maroon undersides, a more strongly silvered effect than the plain species. Airy, open clusters of small white flowers rise well above the foliage on tall slender stems in summer, and long, strawberry-like red runners tipped with plantlets spread the mat outward. It makes a fast-spreading, low groundcover for woodland gardens, shaded borders, and containers where its runners can trail over an edge.

common_name: Nezu Jinja Strawberry Begonia (Large-Leaf Japanese Selection)

planting.note: Plant divisions or rooted stolons in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to full shade; this vigorous, large-leaved selection fills in faster than the typical species.

directions: Plant divisions or rooted stolons in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to full shade. Named for Nezu Shrine in Tokyo's Bunkyo district, where it was found growing wild, this selection produces notably oversized, fuzzy, textured leaves to about 6 inches wide, roughly twice the size of the typical 2-3 inch species leaf, with a green base highlighted by an intricate pattern of silver veins. It is also more vigorous than the species, soon forming a solid mat via fine red stolons tipped with plantlets. In late spring, foot-tall panicles of small white flowers rise above the foliage like a cloud of tiny birds. A bold, fast-covering choice for woodland edges and shaded groundcover plantings where its larger scale can stand out.

common_name: Wildwood Premier Hardy Begonia (Red-Veined Foliage Selection)

planting.note: Plant tubers or divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Wildwood Premier is grown chiefly for foliage color that is more pronounced than the species.

directions: Plant tubers or divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Wildwood Premier is a hardy begonia selection grown for its large, ovate, olive-green leaves, in which the red venation and bright red leaf undersides typical of the species are intensified, with red coloring penetrating through to the veins on the upper leaf surface as well. It forms a bushy, clump-forming mound of foliage to about 2 feet tall on branching stems, bearing pendant clusters of pink flowers from midsummer into fall. Like other hardy begonias it dies back to the ground after frost and returns reliably from tubers and self-sown aerial bulbils the following spring.
